questions.question: Does [clone] work in Purr Data?
questions.notes: Separates what the documentation establishes (clone is described in the Vanilla manual and the IEM object reference) from what it does not (Purr Data's bundling and compatibility), and says the fork's own docs are the place to confirm. Should not assert that it does or does not work there.

questions.question: What is the difference between Pd Vanilla and Pd-extended?
questions.notes: Uses the manual's 'Other flavors' section: Vanilla is the official distribution by Miller Puckette; Pd-extended was a flavor with a large external collection, discontinued in 2014; many tutorials assume it and need their libraries installed; the current flavors are listed on puredata.info.

questions.question: A tutorial I'm following uses [cyclone] objects. Will they work out of the box in Pd Vanilla?
questions.notes: Explains that library objects are externals, not part of Vanilla, and have to be installed/loaded (Externals chapter); suggests checking the object reference for the exact name; does not guarantee the library object behaves like a Vanilla object of a similar name.

questions.question: Which Pd should I install: Vanilla, Purr Data, or PlugData?
questions.notes: Gives the documented baseline (Vanilla is what the manual covers) and the documented fork pattern (GUI changes, pre-installed externals, PlugData as a DAW plugin), points to puredata.info for the active flavors, and marks any recommendation as a suggestion rather than a documented fact.

questions.question: This patch works on my friend's machine but not mine — they use Purr Data and I'm on Pd Vanilla. Why?
questions.notes: Treats the flavor/external difference as the first hypothesis: which objects are library externals, whether they are installed and declared, and GUI-only features. Should ask for the failing object or console error rather than guessing at a specific Purr Data difference.

questions.question: Is Pd-extended still maintained? A forum post told me to download it.
questions.notes: States from the manual that Pd-extended was discontinued in 2014, that tutorials based on it are outdated but can be followed by installing the needed libraries, and points to puredata.info for current flavors.

questions.question: Can I run Pd inside my DAW as a plugin?
questions.notes: Cites the manual's note that PlugData runs Pd as a plugin in a DAW; frames details beyond that (formats, hosts) as unverified and points to PlugData's own docs.

questions.question: Is [expr] part of Pd Vanilla or is it an external I need to install?
questions.notes: Checks the object reference: if the excerpts include an [expr] page, says it is documented in the Vanilla reference; avoids claiming installation steps not in the docs.

questions.question: What is Pd-L2Ork and how does it relate to Purr Data?
questions.notes: Presents Pd-L2Ork and Purr Data as forks of Pd, says the documentation covers Vanilla and does not describe their internals, and points to their own documentation; does not invent history or features.

questions.question: Where is the 'Preferences' menu in Purr Data? I can't find the audio settings.
questions.notes: Says the docs describe Vanilla's interface, cannot verify Purr Data's menus, gives the Vanilla location only as Vanilla, and points to Purr Data's documentation; does not invent menu items.

questions.question: A tutorial uses an object called [mtof~]. Is that built in?
questions.notes: Searches the object name; if the reference has a page it is documented Vanilla, otherwise says the reference does not cover it and it may be an external; does not guess.

questions.question: How do I install an external library like ELSE or zexy in Pd Vanilla?
questions.notes: Uses the manual's Externals chapter (Deken / Find externals, declare/paths as documented) and avoids inventing commands; notes library objects are not guaranteed to behave like Vanilla objects.

questions.question: If I make a patch in PlugData, will it open in Pd Vanilla?
questions.notes: Says forks may introduce incompatibilities and lag behind Vanilla (manual), so it depends on the objects used: externals bundled by the fork must be installed in Vanilla; cannot verify PlugData specifics; suggests testing.

questions.question: Does the Pd manual you're using apply to Purr Data as well?
questions.notes: Quotes the manual's scope: it covers Pd Vanilla; for fully compatible forks it mostly applies; some forks are incompatible; points to the fork's own docs for differences.

questions.question: Why does a Pd-extended patch from 2012 show lots of objects that couldn't be created when I open it in Pd Vanilla?
questions.notes: Explains Pd-extended bundled many externals that Vanilla does not ship; install the libraries the patch uses (Externals chapter) or replace the objects; flags any Vanilla equivalent as a suggestion.
